title: Space-efficient alphabet reduction
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an injection, let $D$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every binary string $x$, the machine $D$ computes the letterwise image under $e$ of the one-symbol output indicating whether $x\in L$, on input the letterwise image of $x$; and suppose that for every $\Gamma$-string $y$ and every time $t$, its computation from input $y$ uses at most $S(|y|)$ space. Then there are a natural number $c$ and a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet that decides $L$ using at most $c(S(n)+1)$ space on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Gamma$ is finite and has decidable equality
$e$ is an injection from the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$
$D$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$L$ is a language of binary strings
$S$ is a natural-number-valued function on natural numbers
For each binary input, $D$ computes the encoded membership-indicator output on the encoded input within some time
For every $\Gamma$-input and every time, $D$ uses space at most $S$ of the input length
